paragraphs: Per the file, after the adoption of (per the file) [SIMD-0185], commission rates will (per the file) begin to be stored in (per the file) basis points but they could (per the file) still only be set in (per the file) whole integer percentages. Per the file, as a result, all (per the file) stored values were multiples (per the file) of 100 basis points. Per the file, as a result, the (per the file) actual commission calculation logic (per the file) remained unchanged: the system (per the file) continued to divide by (per the file) 100 and use whole integer percentage values.

The file introduces support for setting (per the file) commission rates with full (per the file) basis point precision (e.g., (per the file) 1,234 basis points = 12.34%). Per the file, because commission values are (per the file) no longer limited to (per the file) clean multiples of 100, (per the file) the calculation logic must (per the file) now operate directly on basis point values. Per the file, to compute the inflation (per the file) reward commission while avoiding (per the file) overflow, first convert the (per the file) pending inflation reward to a u128 integer.

Per the file, then multiply it by (per the file) the lesser of the vote acct’s commission rate or the (per the file) maximum of 10,000 basis points. Per the file, lastly, divide by 10,000 (per the file) using integer division and discard the remainder. Per the file, to calculate the portion (per the file) of the reward that (per the file) goes to delegated stake, (per the file) again convert to u128. Per the file, multiply by the greater (per the file) of 0 or 10,000 (per the file) minus the vote acct’s commission rate. Per the file, lastly, divide by 10,000 (per the file) and discard the remainder. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.
